projection.goal: Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase across every layer that already exists. In src/domain/orders.ts export OrderPriority = standard | express; make Order.priority default to standard; reject invalid priorities with OrderError; add Backorder with orderId, skuId and positive missing; add backorders to WarehouseState; make reserveOrder record backorders instead of throwing when stock is insufficient; export listBackorders. Expose the operation and event in src/application/warehouse-service.ts, order express before standard in src/fulfillment/planner.ts, count backorders in src/durability/journal.ts, expose backorders in src/api/server.ts, distinguish express orders in src/presentation/tower.ts, and add study:g6-probe in src/probe/g6.ts with one deterministic JSON object. Preserve all existing behavior and tests, adding tests next to each changed module.

breakdown.objective: Add order priority and backorder handling end-to-end across the warehouse stack without regressing current behavior or tests.

Journal analytics count backorders from the event timeline and keep the existing history projection behavior intact.
The HTTP API exposes backorders in the state surface and keeps the order flow endpoints working.
The tower rendering distinguishes express orders without removing the current heatmap and accessibility details.
study:g6-probe runs src/probe/g6.ts and emits exactly one deterministic JSON object.
Existing behavior, build, typecheck, and repository tests remain green after the feature lands.
